To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cluster recovery with oracle queries can be solved in polynomial time for convex clusters, that it can be solved in near-optimal time for general clusterings, that it can always be solved with a logarithmic number of queries for margin-based clusterings, and that margin-based clusterings can always be recovered with $O(\text{log } n)$ queries.

(1) cluster margins are a powerful tool for designing active cluster recovery algorithms that are near-optimal in a wide variety of settings, and (2) cluster margins can be computed using only $O(n\log n)$ queries to an oracle.

(1) the margin between convex clusters in $\mathbb R^m$ is $\Omega(\frac{1}{\sqrt m})$, (2) the margin between clusters with no shape assumptions is $\Omega(1)$, and (3) the margin between concept clusters is $\Omega(\log n)$, and is $\Theta(\log n)$ in many natural concept classes.
